question: On 12 December 2023, the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) granted interim measures (Rule 39) with regard to two Afghan single mothers and their five minor children who were residing in completely unsuitable and unsafe conditions in the closed controlled access center (CCAC) of Kos, which has been funded by the EU.

On 19 September 2023, the ECtHR had also granted interim measures (application 34712/23) on account of the unsuitable living conditions to which asylum applicants in the similarly EU-funded CCAC of Samos were subjected.

In the light of the EU Ombudswoman’s own-initiative strategic inquiry into how the Commission ensures respect for fundamental rights in EU-funded migration management facilities in Greece (CASE OI/3/2022/MHZ)1 and the Ombudswoman’s relevant decision2, which inter alia highlight the ‘detention-like nature’ of these facilities and recommend an ex-post fundamental rights impact assessment, 1.
What is the Commission’s assessment on the ongoing fundamental rights concerns raised vis-àvis the conditions prevailing in EU-funded CCACs?
Does the Commission consider that the Greek islands are under what could be perceived as a situation of ‘migratory pressure’?
What measures does it aim to take to ensure that these recurrent concerns are addressed, including in the context of the common European asylum system?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.8.2024) 1. A steady increase in arrivals on the Greek islands in the second half of 2023 has contributed to a challenging situation as regards reception capacity1. The Commission and the EU agencies support Greece financially and operationally to address these migratory challenges.

This includes, for instance, support to increase transfers to the mainland, a new call for a comprehensive health support project2 and assistance towards an improved system for the swift registration of applications for international protection, in line with EU law.

Consistently with the EU Ombudsman’s suggestions3, the Commission also worked with the Greek authorities to put in place a fundamental rights monitoring mechanism. 2. The Commission acknowledges the difficult circumstances Greece is experiencing. The Asylum and Migration Management Regulation4, adopted as part of the Pact on Migration and Asylum, includes a definition of ‘migratory pressure’.

Following the entry into application of the Pact in June 2026, the Commission will adopt annual reports assessing the migratory situation in the EU and identifying Member States under migratory pressure. 3.

The new Reception Conditions Directive5, also adopted as part of the Pact, will give more prominence to how Member States organise their reception systems, by introducing possibilities and clarifying the actions Member States can undertake to manage their reception capabilities, including mechanisms to assess and address the needs of the national reception systems and allocation of applicants to a specific geographical area or accommodation.

It is key that, as part of the implementation of the Pact, Member State transpose these possibilities in their national legislation and make full use of them to have efficient, rights-based and wellorganised reception systems.
1 Indicatively, beginning of July 2023, 2,053 people were hosted in the Temporary Facility of Mavrovouni, while

as of February 2024 almost 6,000 asylum seekers and beneficiaries of international protection are hosted in the same facility. Similarly, in Kos, there has been a 400% increase of people residing in the reception facility, from 565 in July to 2,818 in February 2024. The average number of arrivals in the Greek islands from 1 January to 21 February 2024 is 120 arrivals per day.

Detailed information on the numbers of persons residing in the accommodation facilities on the Aegean islands are published by the Ministry for Migration & Asylum and are available on: https://migration.gov.gr/en/statistika/ 2 https://tamey.gov.gr/amif-2021-2027/calls/031/ 3 https://www.ombudsman.europa.eu/en/case/en/62000 4 Regulation (EU) 2024/1351. 5 Directive (EU)2024/1346.
